meta_reflection: An operational retro is only as trustworthy as the timing breadcrumbs it is handed; for the seventh milestone running, the detector handed this retro a zero that the on-disk changelog contradicts, so the honest efficiency verdict is 'no analyzable signal' and no wall-time saving is claimed. The load-bearing lesson is process: a fix asserted complete in a prior milestone has gone two milestones without taking effect on the live feed, which is exactly the kind of unverified-fix drift a detector-independent self-check would have caught immediately.
